name: Men's rights movement
summary: The men's rights movement holds that law, courts and social institutions disadvantage men and boys, and campaigns on issues such as child custody and child support, false accusations, male-only conscription, domestic violence against men, male suicide and health, and routine infant circumcision. It generally rejects feminism and the claim that society systematically privileges men. It is a loose, largely online and single-issue movement with no economic or wider political programme.
scope: The contemporary English-language men's rights movement as described on Wikipedia and in coverage of its conferences, drawing on its fathers' rights groups, A Voice for Men and Warren Farrell's work. Because it has no doctrine beyond gender issues, most answers outside gender, family and conscription are low-confidence. It excludes the earlier men's liberation movement, and the separatist MGTOW and pickup-artist strands are noted only as variants.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The movement does not take a stance on healthcare systems; it only complains about funding gaps such as prostate cancer research versus women's health, which cuts both ways.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the movement's issue lists touches ownership of industry; adherents are split along general political lines.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No stated position; adherents' tax views vary with their general politics, not their men's-rights stance.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not a topic in the movement's literature, though complaints about alimony and asset division in divorce hint at some property sympathy; adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Activists criticise welfare and child support as favouring women, but also demand men's services and benefits, so there is no clear line.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented stance on surveillance; adherents vary.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement has no drug policy beyond complaints about harsher male sentencing; adherents are split.

limit-guns.rationale: No movement position; adherents differ by national and political background.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not a core issue and adherents are split between sexual-liberty and traditionalist views.

rehabilitation.rationale: The movement complains of harsher sentences for men but has no stated penal philosophy.

traditional-family.rationale: Fathers' rights wings stress fathers' involvement and shared parenting, but the movement also attacks marriage law as unfair to men and MGTOW rejects marriage; adherents are genuinely split. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

abortion-legal.rationale: The movement debates male reproductive choice ('paper abortion') and paternal notification, but has no shared view on legality of abortion itself.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Activists dispute feminist claims that gender roles are imposed, and some cite innate sex differences, though the sources describe this only in passing; adherents vary. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement seeks policy reform through courts and legislatures but has no stated view on pace of change.

democracy-best.rationale: The movement operates within democratic politics but also contains strands that reject electoral participation (MGTOW) or women's suffrage rhetoric; AVFM disavows the latter. No clear position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mainstream adherents claim equality for men not rule by a natural elite; critics allege male supremacy in some groups, but the typical adherent claims equal treatment.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The movement is largely secular and online; no scripture-based programme is documented, though some religious fathers' groups exist.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Activists present their case as one of rights and equal treatment (conscription, custody) and object to duties imposed on men alone, such as the draft and child support.

restore-past-order.rationale: Critics such as Allan call the movement reactionary and others say it opposes a more equal gender order, but adherents claim to seek equality, not restoration; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No sign of primitivism in the movement.

taxation-theft.rationale: No documented position, though some libertarian-leaning adherents say so; split.

harm-principle.rationale: No stated view; adherents want legal protection from false accusations and compelled child support but are split on broader state limits.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement claims equal individual rights for men and boys and targets group-based preferences for women, but also advocates sex-based categories such as 'men's rights' and fathers' groups; split. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

exit-over-voice.rationale: MGTOW stresses withdrawal from society but this is not about leaving a country; no position.

media-academia-power.rationale: Activists commonly claim that academia and media are dominated by feminist perspectives that marginalise men's issues, which a Hatewatch report on a men's issues conference reflects in its account of speakers. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: No sign of feudal ideas in the movement.

school-vouchers.rationale: No documented position, though some activists want single-sex classes and alternatives to mainstream schooling for boys; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Online strands often present themselves as rationalist, but religious fathers' groups exist; no shared position.

work-for-welfare.rationale: No documented position, though the movement criticises benefits systems for favouring women; split.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Mainstream adherents demand equal legal treatment of men (custody, conscription, domestic-violence services) and attack sex-based legal distinctions, though some strands are traditionalist; the core framing is anti-discrimination.

elite-replacement.rationale: No documented position; some manosphere figures touch this theme but it is not part of the movement's agenda.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Activists say patriarchy is a myth and that women hold as much or more power than men; the movement's premise is that men are not privileged relative to women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: No documented position, though activists distrust politicians they see as pandering to feminist lobbies; split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: No documented position; the movement seeks state action on family law and male services, but adherents include libertarians.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of the movement; its stated aims do not include discouraging mixed relationships.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality before the law between men and women is the movement's stated basis, though critics say some strands treat women as lesser; typical adherent claims equal rights.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: No documented position, though some manosphere strands endorse competition; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement is decentralised and has no vanguard organisation.

clerical-rule.rationale: No sign of clerical politics in the movement.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No sign of this in the movement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No documented position, though activists criticise academia; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: No documented position; adherents are split between libertarian and traditionalist views.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Activists oppose routine infant circumcision, which many religious communities practise, but the movement states no general view on religious exemptions from law.

sacred-ruler.rationale: No sign of this in the movement.

equal-parenting.rationale: Default equal or joint custody is the central demand of the fathers' rights wing, the main route into the movement.

common-currency.rationale: The movement is indifferent to monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement is indifferent to supranational unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The movement is indifferent to minority autonomy.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The movement opposes feminist quota policies as unequal treatment, though sources document this mainly in general terms.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement has no trade programme.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The movement has no trade programme.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Activists want anti-discrimination law applied to men while many libertarian-leaning members oppose it; adherents are split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No documented position, though activists invoke equal rights under law and are split on constitutional design.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is organized around political and legal campaigns, so withdrawal is contrary to it, though the MGTOW strand withdraws from relationships.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Many in the movement hold that media and culture promote misandry and a feminist social order; this is an inference from its critique of media.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The movement's core claim is that boys and men face neglected disadvantage in education, health and suicide, and Farrell's work centers on this.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence against men is a named issue area for the movement, which demands equal recognition and services.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Activists complain about divorce courts, alimony and custody outcomes but split on easy divorce itself, so no stated position.

job-guarantee.rationale: No economic doctrine; adherents range from libertarian to left, so the movement is indifferent.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents complain that courts and laws are biased against men, but no general stance on a duty to obey is documented.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the movement's platform; its grievances target feminism and family law, not a minority's plot, though fringe voices differ.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Adherents are split: fathers' rights groups want fairer marriage and divorce law, while some voices urge men to avoid marriage.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is loose and largely online, but fathers' rights groups also form lasting organisations, so adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The movement is single-issue on gender; the sources discuss no economic ownership position.

defeat-communism.rationale: No anti-communism or foreign-policy stance is documented; the movement is a loose gender-issue movement.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and the claim that women are systematically subordinated, so a feminist case for economic transformation is rejected. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and the claim that society systematically privileges men, which this framework presupposes. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

assisted-dying.rationale: Male suicide is a campaign issue but the sources give no stance on assisted dying, so adherents are treated as split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement has no position on this; members are mixed and it is not on the agenda.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The movement has no foreign-policy position.

reification.rationale: The movement has no economic doctrine; a Marxist theory of reification is foreign to a movement that mostly rejects structural critiques of society.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement claims equal rights for men and women and has no racial platform; coverage of its conferences records no such restriction. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

online-participation.rationale: The movement is largely online, but it has no stated position on internet voting or deliberation.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The movement is organised around gender and has no religious-minority agenda; boycotts of minority-owned shops are not part of it, and adherents would disavow them.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement has no position on constitutional design for ethnic or sectarian divisions; adherents are split and it is outside its gender focus.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Adherents are split between market-minded and welfare-supporting views, and the movement's own complaints concern unequal services for men, not who should deliver aid.

vote-delegation.rationale: The movement has no position on delegated voting; this is outside its programme and adherents are split.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The movement does not discuss extinction risk; its concern with male suicide and health is a different priority, so adherents are split or indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents are split, with secular equal-treatment advocates alongside religious traditionalists; the movement takes no line on religious offices.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement has no position on immigration or resident voting; adherents are split.

family-wage.rationale: Adherents criticize the male provider burden but the movement takes no line on a family wage.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement objects to male-only conscription but takes no stance on when wars are justified.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and the claim that women's values deserve special weight; it argues men are the group left unheard.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The movement has no stated line on gun control or armed groups; its gender-issue focus leaves adherents split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: It has no economic programme, and adherents range from libertarian to centrist.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm policy is outside the movement's concerns and its largely online supporters are split on economics, so this is a neutral inference.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The movement takes no line on defence; nothing in its sources addresses nuclear arms, so adherents are treated as split.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The movement has no environmental programme and its libertarian and conservative wings would split on this; no stance is documented.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Adherents complain of harsh sentencing of men and false accusations, which points against rigid rules, yet many are tough-on-crime conservatives; split.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Immigration is outside the movement's scope and its supporters are politically mixed; no stance is documented.

premarital-sex.rationale: A Voice for Men and Farrell argue against the double standard that stigmatises sexual freedom for women while ignoring men's, and treat sexual choice as the same for both sexes. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: A Voice for Men and Farrell reject the feminist view that women are systemically oppressed, and treat religion as not a major cause. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and campaigns against women-only state programmes and agencies, arguing they ignore male disadvantage and so are one-sided.

equal-conscription.rationale: Male-only conscription is one of the movement's named campaign issues, and its demand is equal treatment of men and women under any draft.

close-ties-china.rationale: The movement has no foreign or economic programme beyond gender issues.

missingStatements.text: Courts should presume that children of separated parents spend equal time with each parent.
missingStatements.rationale: Joint custody as the default is the central demand of the fathers' rights wing, the main route into the movement.

missingStatements.text: Men and women should be treated identically in law on military conscription.
missingStatements.rationale: The male-only draft is framed as sex discrimination by the movement; adherents want it ended or extended to women.
missingStatements.declined: The existing conscription statement covers the draft question and a male-only-draft statement is too narrow to keep the bank lean.

missingStatements.text: Routine circumcision of infant boys for non-medical reasons should be banned.
missingStatements.rationale: Most members oppose it and compare it to female genital mutilation, and bodily autonomy is a listed issue area.
missingStatements.declined: Infant circumcision is a narrow single-issue topic with low inclusion across ideologies.

missingStatements.text: A man should be able to avoid legal parenthood for a child he did not choose to father, including by testing paternity or opting out before birth.
missingStatements.rationale: Paternity testing, relief from support for non-biological children and 'paper abortion' are advocated, with paternity listed among core issues.
missingStatements.declined: Paternity opt-out and "paper abortion" is a niche demand within the movement; too narrow for the bank.

missingStatements.text: Women's violence against men in intimate relationships is as significant as men's violence against women and deserves equal shelter and services.
missingStatements.rationale: Activists claim near-symmetry in domestic violence and campaign for shelters for abused men.

notes: Fringe strands (MGTOW, red pill) and the groups the SPLC listed as male supremacist would answer gender questions more extremely; critics argue the movement is defined by backlash against feminism. Almost every non-gender answer is an inference, so the profile may fail the inclusion check.
